Integrating the derivative of \(x^{2k+1}(L^2-x^2)p\), \(k=0,1\), gives a 2x2 moment system; strict weighted Cauchy–Schwarz gives determinant \(\Delta>0\). Solving reconstructs \(\mu/D\) and \(s/D\) exactly. A standalone 65-decimal-digit checker passed 26 finite diagnostics; universal proof is analytic, not finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The explicit reflected noisy-pitchfork sign divider at fixed variance, impossibility from variance alone, and boundary-annihilating rational four-even-moment formula are not statements found in the inspected primary work. Sanders et al. derive time-increment regression for unreflected cubic dynamics; Miyazawa supplies general reflected stationary densities (a known premise, not claimed new); Pavliotis–Zanoni supply polynomial-diffusion moment systems on an unbounded state space. Broad exponential-family identifiability is old and is not itself claimed novel; the explicit curve and reflected boundary-free inverse formula provide the narrower contribution. Hu et al. and Hu–Xi cover reflected linear OU rather than cubic. Remaining broader priority risks are identified.
residual_risks: The global mean-parameter injectivity is a known general exponential-family corollary, and is excluded from novel priority; exact sign-curve coordinates might also be in earlier references.
Further reflected nonlinear diffusion inverse-problem literature could include the same boundary-zero polynomial formula; historical search is not exhaustive.

value.rationale: The motivating problem is to classify the cubic criticality of a noisy pitchfork. Reflection provides a natural confined regime in which both cubic signs admit a true equilibrium law, unlike the escaping unconfined subcritical system. An exact sign boundary using only two stationary even moments and a parameter-free eighth-moment rational certificate identify criticality without temporal differentiation, noise-scale calibration or boundary local-time measurement. The variance-only impossibility is sharp, and the explicit formula is independently usable for state-only diagnostics. The claim is restricted to a structural inverse problem; it makes no false empirical finite-sample or global tipping assertions.
